record: P4S-31D-4/5 — mobile voice compile (native mobile app + mobile browser)
activation: NOT AUTHORIZED — this artifact plans P4S-31D-4 (mobile app push-to-talk) and P4S-31D-5 (mobile browser tap-to-talk). No voice implementation, wiring, or rollout is authorized by this file. Both packets remain hard-held until the owner explicitly starts them, after P4S-31D-1..3 per the contract sequence.
doctrine: Voice is a thin adapter into Cockpit Chat. A mobile utterance becomes a transcript that enters the SAME rail as typed text: sendMessage(text, 'voice', routing, voice_turn_id) -> POST /advisor/converse -> deterministic classify_intent -> governed intent loop -> held gate -> approve -> PROOF_RECORDED. Mobile adds NO new execution path, NO new auth surface, NO new intent classifier.

agrees_with.statement: This compile DEEPENS the matrix verdicts for the two mobile targets; it contradicts nothing. Where the matrix says NOT_FEASIBLE or CONSTRAINED, this plan repeats the verdict verbatim and designs inside it.

owner_observation_2026_07_06.event: The owner pressed push-to-talk on a MOBILE BROWSER and received the consent-required refusal (typed CONSENT_REQUIRED, mic never opened).
owner_observation_2026_07_06.reading: Correct fail-closed behavior. Capture must not open without an active VoiceConsentGrant(push_to_talk) for that device — the refusal is the contract working, not a bug.
owner_observation_2026_07_06.gap: The consent-grant UX was not reachable from the refusal on a small viewport. That consent UX gap is being closed in Lane A; it is a presentation gap, not a contract gap.
owner_observation_2026_07_06.implication_for_this_plan: Mobile surfaces MUST render the grant path inside the refusal itself (inline consent affordance on the CONSENT_REQUIRED outcome), sized for a small viewport. Mobile browser PTT remains CONSTRAINED per the matrix — iOS Safari drops the mic on tab background / screen lock.

native_ios.capture_api: AVAudioEngine tap on inputNode (PCM16 16kHz mono) under AVAudioSession category .playAndRecord; SFSpeechRecognizer consumes the same buffer for on-device STT
native_ios.tap_to_talk_semantics: Explicit mic button. Tap opens capture (after consent + TCC checks), tap again or VAD end-of-speech stops it. Capture runs ONLY while the app is foreground-active. No hold-to-talk requirement — toggle semantics avoid gesture-recognizer conflicts.
native_ios.breaks_on_background_lock: App backgrounded or device locked -> AVAudioSession is interrupted and capture ends (no 'audio' UIBackgroundMode is claimed — a non-audio utility app claiming it is an App Review rejection risk and would contradict the matrix). The adapter treats interruption as session end: stop capture, discard buffers, emit typed CAPTURE_ENDED state. Resume requires a fresh tap in the foreground.
native_ios.stt: on-device SFSpeechRecognizer preferred (requiresOnDeviceRecognition where the locale supports it); server STT fallback per battery_privacy_constraints

native_android.tap_to_talk_semantics: Same toggle tap-to-talk as iOS: tap opens capture behind consent + RECORD_AUDIO runtime grant, tap/VAD end stops it. Foreground activity only.
native_android.breaks_on_background_lock: Activity pause / screen lock -> capture stops. Android 10+ blocks microphone access for backgrounded apps without a microphone-type foreground service, and P4S-31D-4 ships NO foreground service — push-to-talk is strictly foreground. Adapter emits typed CAPTURE_ENDED and requires a fresh tap.
native_android.stt: on-device android.speech.SpeechRecognizer preferred (EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE where supported); server STT fallback per battery_privacy_constraints

mobile_safari.capture_api: web getUserMedia -> PCM16 16kHz over the existing authenticated WS (same protocol as cockpit/src/renderer/api/voice-ws.ts)
mobile_safari.tap_to_talk_semantics: Tap-to-talk TOGGLE, not press-and-hold: getUserMedia and AudioContext.resume() must run inside a direct user gesture, and long-press fires iOS text-selection/callout behaviors. First tap in a session must also unlock audio output for TTS (same gesture chain).
mobile_safari.breaks_on_background_lock: Tab background or screen lock -> WebKit ends the mic track immediately and freezes timers; the WS may be dropped by proxy idle timeout. The adapter treats MediaStreamTrack 'ended' as session end: typed CAPTURE_ENDED, no buffered audio replayed, no auto-reacquire — a new user gesture is required on return to foreground. This is the graceful-refusal requirement of P4S-31D-5.
mobile_safari.note: All iOS browsers (Chrome/Firefox/Edge on iOS) use WebKit — these constraints apply to every browser on iOS, not just Safari-branded.

mobile_chrome.capture_api: web getUserMedia -> PCM16 16kHz over the existing authenticated WS (same voice-ws.ts protocol)
mobile_chrome.tap_to_talk_semantics: Same toggle tap-to-talk as mobile Safari for cross-surface parity. Mic permission is per-origin and persistable on Android Chrome, so re-prompts are rarer than iOS.
mobile_chrome.breaks_on_background_lock: Backgrounded tab is throttled and capture is suspended/stopped shortly after; screen lock stops capture. Although Android Chrome is more permissive than WebKit, the adapter applies the SAME policy as mobile_safari: track end or visibilitychange-to-hidden ends the session with a typed CAPTURE_ENDED. No background capture is attempted on any mobile browser.

mobile_browser_limitations.autoplay_policy: TTS audio playback requires a prior user gesture to unlock the output element/AudioContext. The first PTT tap doubles as the unlock; TTS received before unlock is queued or dropped with a typed TTS_BLOCKED state — never a silent failure.
mobile_browser_limitations.mic_policy: Mic permission is per-origin. iOS Safari grants are effectively ephemeral (frequent re-prompts; 'remember' behavior varies by version) — the adapter must treat every session start as potentially needing a fresh browser prompt, in addition to the UMH VoiceConsentGrant. Both layers required; either missing = fail-closed refusal.
mobile_browser_limitations.ws_keepalive: A backgrounded mobile tab freezes JS timers, so WS ping/pong stops and the nginx proxy (/api/umh/voice/ws -> 127.0.0.1:8096/voice) idle-times the socket out. Policy: do NOT fight this. On visibility loss, end the capture session cleanly (mic_stop). On return to foreground, reconnect the WS lazily on the next user gesture. Never buffer or replay audio across a reconnect.
mobile_browser_limitations.pwa_constraints: Installing the cockpit as a PWA changes nothing about mic policy on iOS: no background execution, no service-worker microphone, getUserMedia only in the active window, capture dies on lock. A PWA install is a UX nicety (icon, standalone chrome), not a capability upgrade. Wake word and ambient remain NOT_FEASIBLE on mobile browser exactly as the matrix records.
mobile_browser_limitations.consent_ux_small_viewport: Per the 2026-07-06 owner observation: the CONSENT_REQUIRED refusal must carry its own resolution path on a small viewport — an inline 'enable push-to-talk on this device' affordance rendered with the refusal (thumb-reachable, no desktop settings rail required). Grant/revoke round-trips the same /voice/consent surface the desktop adapter uses. Lane A owns the consent UX fix; this plan consumes it.

info_plist: NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription — mandatory when SFSpeechRecognizer (on-device STT) is used
ios.tcc: Microphone and Speech Recognition are SEPARATE TCC prompts. Both must be granted for the on-device STT path. Either denied -> typed refusal with a deep link to Settings; the adapter never retries silently.
ios.background_modes: NONE claimed. No 'audio' UIBackgroundMode. Claiming background audio to keep the mic alive would be an App Review rejection risk for a non-audio utility app and would contradict the matrix ios_background NOT_FEASIBLE verdict.

manifest: RECORD_AUDIO — dangerous permission, requested at runtime
INTERNET — transcript POST + optional server-STT WS
android.runtime_flow: Request RECORD_AUDIO on the FIRST push-to-talk tap, never at install/launch. Denial -> typed refusal; permanent denial ('don't ask again') -> refusal with a Settings deep link.
android.foreground_service_types: NOT shipped in P4S-31D-4. Push-to-talk is strictly foreground and needs no service. If the owner ever approves the CONSTRAINED Android-background slice (separate, owner-gated, post-privacy-review), it would require FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE permissions, android:foregroundServiceType="microphone" (mandatory on Android 14+), and a persistent user-visible notification. Recording that requirement here is documentation of the constraint, not a plan to build it.

background_ambient_feasibility.statement: This compile PROMISES NO mobile ambient or background listening. The verdicts below restate the platform_voice_feasibility_matrix.json rows verbatim; any mobile ambient work is deferred behind a platform spike + privacy review + explicit owner sign-off (P4S-31D-6 scope, desktop-first).

ios_background.why: iOS does not permit continuous background microphone for a non-audio utility app; background audio mode + App Review policy block it. No compliant always-on-mic path today.

ios_foreground_ambient.why: Foreground ambient only, screen-on, under explicit VoiceConsentGrant. Not scheduled by these packets.

android_background.why: Possible only via a microphone-type foreground service (persistent notification, Android 14 FGS type declaration), user-visible and battery-costly. Deferred and owner-gated; NOT scheduled by these packets.

android_foreground_ambient.why: Foreground ambient feasible under consent; not scheduled by these packets.

mobile_browser_wake_word.why: No background execution; tabs are suspended and the mic is released; iOS WebKit has no service-worker background audio and no wake-word API.

mobile_browser_ambient.why: Same as wake word: no background mic, tab suspension, screen lock releases capture. Explicitly NOT promised.

on_device_stt_preferred.ios: SFSpeechRecognizer with requiresOnDeviceRecognition where the locale supports it — audio never leaves the device on this path

battery_privacy_constraints.server_stt_fallback: Only for surfaces/locales without on-device STT (and the whole mobile-browser surface, which has no on-device STT today): the existing voice_server (Groq Whisper + faster-whisper fallback) over the AUTHENTICATED channel only — wss:// through the nginx /api/umh/voice/ws proxy under the operator's session. No unauthenticated audio endpoint, ever.
battery_privacy_constraints.cloud_transcription: DEFERRED to a privacy review, unchanged from docs/VOICE_INTENT_CONTRACT.md. This plan does not decide it.
battery_privacy_constraints.no_audio_persistence: Capture buffers live inside the adapter only. Only TranscriptEvent text crosses the chat seam (carries_audio=false, always). No audio is stored on device or server by default.
battery_privacy_constraints.battery: No wake runtime on mobile in these packets. The audio pipeline (session, tap/recorder, WS) exists only between capture start and stop and is fully torn down on stop. Ambient listening is battery-hostile on mobile and is not scheduled — consistent with the matrix risk notes.
battery_privacy_constraints.secrets: STT/TTS provider credentials stay in the existing secret runtime (1Password op run) on the server side. No provider key ever ships in a mobile client or this artifact.

adapter_into_cockpit_chat.interface: The ONE PlatformVoiceAdapter interface from docs/VOICE_INTENT_CONTRACT.md — requestConsent, openSession, startCapture, stopCapture, closeSession; events onTranscript, onWake (unused on mobile: no wake mode), onError, onStateChange. Reference implementation: cockpit/src/renderer/api/platform-voice-adapter.ts (desktop browser, P4S-31D-1).
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.output_seam: Adapter output is ONLY a chat message: sendMessage(text, source='voice', routing, voice_turn_id) -> POST /advisor/converse — the SAME endpoint and body text uses.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.mobile_browser_transport_reuse: P4S-31D-5 reuses the EXISTING PCM16 16kHz WebSocket protocol from cockpit/src/renderer/api/voice-ws.ts verbatim (mic_start/mic_stop control frames, binary PCM16 chunks up, transcript/tts events down). The mobile-browser adapter is the desktop-browser adapter plus mobile lifecycle handling: gesture-gated start, track-'ended' as session end, lazy WS reconnect on foreground, no audio buffering across reconnects.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.mobile_app_transport: P4S-31D-4 prefers on-device STT so no audio leaves the device; when the server-STT fallback is used it speaks the same PCM16 WS protocol over the authenticated wss channel.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.identity: The mobile Clerk session principal, resolved SERVER-SIDE at /advisor/converse — identical to the principal that stamps decided_by on the ProofRecord. The adapter stamps no identity and cannot spoof one.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.consent: VoiceConsentGrant per-mode per-device: (operator_principal, device_registry_id, activation_mode='push_to_talk'). Mobile devices register in infra/device_registry.json as controller-role entries; the grant is read fail-closed from GET /voice/consent before any capture. Missing/revoked/unreadable -> typed CONSENT_REQUIRED refusal with inline grant affordance (per owner_observation_2026_07_06). A push_to_talk grant never authorizes wake_word or always_on.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.device_role: Mobile surfaces are controller role only — never executor, never orchestrator. The orchestrator-role node never has a microphone.
adapter_into_cockpit_chat.proof_requirements: Per the contract implementation sequence: P4S-31D-4 proof = foreground capture -> transcript -> same rail, identity = mobile Clerk principal. P4S-31D-5 proof = tap -> transcript -> same rail, plus graceful typed refusal on background/lock. Both extend the P4S-31C server-truth chain by one hop; UI rendering alone is not proof.
